docs.title: Placement Syndicate
docs.text:
An AI-enabled placement preparation platform built around microservices, interview knowledge, and grounded resume feedback.

Placement Syndicate brings together placement-preparation resources and an AI-assisted resume analysis workflow. Its documented architecture uses a Spring Boot application for core platform capabilities and a Python FastAPI service for document processing, retrieval, and LLM-backed feedback.

docs.title: What this documentation covers
docs.text:
• The system's main components and their responsibilities.
  • How a resume moves through ingestion, retrieval, LLM synthesis, and report delivery.
  • Why lexical and semantic retrieval are combined.
  • How the services and data stores fit together.
  • Developer-facing API and operational concepts.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Area Technology / responsibility Core backend Java 17, Spring Boot AI service Python, FastAPI Frontend React Relational data PostgreSQL Document / experience data MongoDB Event messaging Kafka and RabbitMQ Authentication Keycloak Retrieval BM25 and Sentence-Transformers LLM inference Groq

docs.title: Primary workflow
docs.text:
1. A student uploads a PDF or DOCX resume.
  2. The AI service extracts text from the document.
  3. The service retrieves relevant interview experiences from the experience catalog.
  4. Retrieved evidence and resume content are passed to the LLM.
  5. The generated feedback is stored and made available to the frontend.

Read the system overview Explore the resume feedback workflow

docs.title: API workflow
docs.text: This page documents the API interactions explicitly identified in the project case study.

docs.title: Resume upload
docs.text:
POST /api/resume/upload

Purpose: submit a PDF or DOCX resume to the FastAPI service for text extraction and downstream analysis.

The frontend upload flow is described in the project case study. Confirm the current request field names, authentication requirements, response schema, and maximum file size from the API implementation or OpenAPI page before integrating another client.

docs.title: Retrieve feedback
docs.text:
GET /api/resume/feedback/{filename}

Purpose: retrieve the generated feedback associated with the uploaded resume filename.

The frontend uses this endpoint to obtain the analysis and display recommendations.

docs.text:
flowchart TD

docs.title: Why separate the AI service?
docs.text: Resume parsing, retrieval, embedding generation, and LLM inference have different dependencies and resource characteristics from ordinary application CRUD operations. Keeping this processing in a dedicated FastAPI service provides a clear boundary for AI-specific logic and lets the core backend evolve independently.

docs.title: Data responsibilities
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL: relational application records.
  • MongoDB: document-oriented records used by the AI workflow, including interview experiences and generated feedback.
  • Kafka and RabbitMQ: asynchronous messaging infrastructure. Their exact event and queue responsibilities should be checked in the service configuration.
  • Keycloak: identity and authentication integration.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
The documented architecture uses two database styles for different data needs:

Store Role PostgreSQL Relational application data MongoDB Document-oriented data used by AI workflows, including interview experiences and resume feedback

The resume-feedback case study specifically identifies MongoDB as the source of the experience collection and the destination for generated feedback records.

docs.title: Messaging
docs.text:
Kafka and RabbitMQ are included in the platform technology stack for asynchronous event messaging.

Messaging can decouple a producer from a consumer: the producer publishes a message, while a separate consumer processes it. This helps services avoid requiring every operation to complete in one synchronous request.

The exact topic names, queue names, event schemas, retry policy, and ownership boundaries are implementation-specific. Consult the current service configuration before publishing or consuming production messages.

docs.title: Data lifecycle: resume feedback
docs.text:
1. Resume file is submitted by the user.
  2. Extracted text is used for retrieval.
  3. Experience records are read from MongoDB.
  4. The LLM produces a feedback report using retrieved context.
  5. Feedback and metadata are persisted in MongoDB.
  6. The frontend requests and displays the stored result.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Placement Syndicate addresses a common placement-preparation problem: students often have to search across disconnected resources for interview experiences, mentorship support, and resume guidance.

The platform combines those capabilities and uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground resume feedback in a catalog of relevant interview experiences.

docs.title: Main service boundaries
docs.text:
Component Responsibility React frontend User-facing workflows, including resume upload and feedback presentation Spring Boot backend Core application and platform-side business capabilities FastAPI AI service Resume text extraction, hybrid retrieval, and LLM inference PostgreSQL Relational application data MongoDB Document-oriented data, including interview experience records and resume feedback Kafka / RabbitMQ Asynchronous messaging between platform components Keycloak Authentication and identity management Groq LLM inference for feedback generation

The exact ownership of individual tables, topics, queues, and deployment settings should be confirmed against the current implementation before operational changes are made.

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• Separate core platform responsibilities from AI-specific processing.
  • Retrieve relevant interview evidence before asking an LLM to generate feedback.
  • Keep the resume-analysis workflow understandable as a sequence of service-level stages.
  • Persist generated feedback so it can be retrieved by the frontend.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning API Application Programming Interface; a defined way for software components to communicate BM25 A lexical ranking function used in information retrieval Embedding A numerical vector representation of text FastAPI A Python framework for building APIs Hybrid search Retrieval that combines lexical and semantic signals LLM Large Language Model MongoDB A document-oriented database PostgreSQL A relational database RAG Retrieval-Augmented Generation; retrieving relevant information before generating a response Spring Boot Java framework for building backend applications Top-k The k highest-ranked retrieval results Sentence-Transformers Models and tooling for producing sentence embeddings Keycloak Identity and access management platform SSE Server-Sent Events; a mechanism for streaming server updates to a client

docs.title: Why hybrid retrieval?
docs.text:
A resume and an interview-experience record may describe the same skill using different words. A keyword-only search can miss that relationship. Conversely, semantic retrieval can overlook exact identifiers such as a company name, framework, or certification.

Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and semantic signals.

docs.title: BM25: lexical matching
docs.text:
BM25 is a ranking method based on term relevance. It is useful when exact words matter, such as:

  • Java
  • Spring Boot
  • PostgreSQL
  • a company name
  • a specific job title

docs.title: Sentence-Transformers: semantic matching
docs.text:
A sentence-transformer model converts text into dense numerical embeddings. Similarity between embeddings can surface conceptually related content even when the exact words differ.

For example, a resume phrase about asynchronous messaging may be relevant to an experience that discusses Kafka or RabbitMQ even if the wording is not identical.

docs.title: Combining the channels
docs.text:
The project case study describes a hybrid search process that combines BM25 and dense semantic retrieval and selects top-k relevant interview experiences. The exact score-normalization and fusion implementation should be checked in the current HybridSearcher source before changing ranking behavior.

flowchart TD
    Q[Resume text] --> L[Lexical retrieval: BM25]
    Q --> E[Embedding generation]
    E --> S[Semantic retrieval]
    L --> F[Combine / rank candidates]
    S --> F
    F --> K[Top-k interview experiences]
    K --> C[Context for LLM]

docs.title: Retrieval quality checklist
docs.text:
• Include representative interview experiences in the catalog.
  • Keep company, role, skill, and technology terms consistent.
  • Inspect retrieved results for relevance, not just whether the search returned results.
  • Evaluate whether top-k results support the feedback being generated.
  • Do not let the LLM introduce claims that are unsupported by the retrieved context.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
The repository contains multiple services and a frontend. Start by following the setup instructions in the root README and the individual service READMEs. Their dependency and startup commands may differ.

A practical startup sequence is:

  1. Review environment-variable examples and service prerequisites.
  2. Start the required databases and message brokers.
  3. Configure Keycloak and the service connection settings.
  4. Start the Spring Boot backend.
  5. Start the FastAPI AI service.
  6. Start the React frontend.
  7. Verify the health and connectivity of each service using the project's documented checks.

docs.title: Configuration safety
docs.text:
• Keep API keys, database credentials, and authentication secrets out of source control.
  • Use environment variables or an approved secrets manager.
  • Do not put real resumes or personal information into unapproved AI tools.
  • Use sanitized test documents when debugging ingestion.
  • Avoid logging full resume text or sensitive user data.

docs.title: Troubleshooting guide
docs.text: Symptom Areas to inspect Resume upload fails File type, request size, frontend API base URL, FastAPI logs No feedback appears Text extraction result, retrieval results, LLM response, persistence Irrelevant feedback Experience catalog quality, lexical/semantic retrieval results, prompt context Database errors Connection settings, credentials, database availability Messaging delays Broker availability, consumer health, queue/topic configuration Authentication failures Keycloak realm/client configuration, token validity, service-side validation

docs.title: Operational verification
docs.text: Before releasing a change, test a representative PDF and DOCX, inspect retrieved experiences, verify that the generated report is persisted, and confirm that the frontend can retrieve and render it.

docs.title: Resume feedback workflow
docs.text: The resume-feedback pipeline connects document ingestion with evidence retrieval and LLM-generated analysis.

docs.title: End-to-end sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor Student
    participant UI as React UI
    participant AI as FastAPI service
    participant DB as MongoDB
    participant Search as HybridSearcher
    participant LLM as Groq LLM

    Student->>UI: Upload PDF / DOCX
    UI->>AI: POST /api/resume/upload
    AI->>AI: Extract resume text
    AI->>DB: Load interview experience catalog
    AI->>Search: Fit / query hybrid search
    Search->>DB: Retrieve relevant experience records
    Search-->>AI: Top-k matching experiences
    AI->>LLM: Resume + retrieved evidence
    LLM-->>AI: Grounded gap-analysis report
    AI->>DB: Store report and metadata
    UI->>AI: GET /api/resume/feedback/{filename}
    AI-->>UI: Feedback result
    UI-->>Student: Display recommendations

docs.title: 1. Resume ingestion
docs.text:
The student uploads a PDF or DOCX through the React interface. The frontend sends the file to the FastAPI endpoint:

POST /api/resume/upload

The service extracts plain text from the uploaded document. This text becomes the query input for the retrieval stage.

docs.title: 2. Experience catalog loading
docs.text: The service loads interview experience records from MongoDB. These records provide the reference material against which resume skills and experience can be compared.

docs.title: 3. Hybrid retrieval
docs.text:
The HybridSearcher uses complementary retrieval approaches:

  • BM25 lexical retrieval identifies exact terms such as company names, technologies, and role-specific keywords.
  • Sentence-Transformers semantic retrieval represents text as embeddings so that conceptually related descriptions can be found even when their wording differs.

The search stage returns the most relevant experience records for the resume.

docs.title: 4. LLM synthesis
docs.text:
The service sends the resume content and retrieved experience evidence to the LLM through a structured prompt. The model generates a gap-analysis report using the retrieved context.

The retrieval stage is important: the LLM is given relevant project-specific evidence instead of being asked to produce recommendations from the resume alone.

docs.title: 5. Persistence and delivery
docs.text:
The generated report and associated metadata are stored in MongoDB, in the resume_feedback collection described by the project case study.

The frontend retrieves the result using:

GET /api/resume/feedback/{filename}

It then displays the feedback to the student.

docs.title: Failure and accuracy considerations
docs.text:
• A file that cannot be parsed should not be treated as an empty or valid resume.
  • Retrieval quality depends on the completeness and quality of the experience catalog.
  • LLM output should be reviewed against the retrieved evidence; generated text is not automatically authoritative.
  • The exact upload limits, supported MIME types, timeout behavior, and error response schema should be verified in the current API implementation.
